# Story 51 — TICKETS-8-API: a customer may act only on their own ticket, on every path (Story: CRM-86)

## Prerequisites

- **TICKETS-1-API (queue and ticket routes)** shipped: the routes under `/tickets/:id` this story guards already exist in `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js` (currently `PATCH /tickets/:id/assignee` at line 50 and `PATCH /tickets/:id/status` at line 63).
- **PLATFORM-4-API (subject resolver / `requireSubject`)** shipped: the route file at `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.routes.js:3` already imports `requireSubject` from `api/src/platform/http/permission.js` and every guarded route attaches `req.subject`.
- Precedent to follow: the audit-guarantee census in `api/src/features/audit/audit.guarantee.test.js` — this story's route-enumeration test uses the same shape.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` before starting (per intake standing hints).
- Coordinate nothing outside `api/`: SC-2 forbids any client-side enforcement, and the intake lists customer portal and reply routes as out of scope.

---

## Story Goal

Enforce, in the API service layer, that a subject whose role is **customer** may act on a ticket **only when that ticket is theirs**. The refusal is indistinguishable from the ticket not existing (same status, same code, same body) so a stranger cannot use the response to confirm somebody else's ticket exists. Enforcement lives **inside the transaction that already reads the ticket** in `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js` — not in the route file, so one rule stays one line.

A route-census test enumerates every route the ticket router serves under `/tickets/:id`, drives each one as a non-owner customer subject, and asserts each one returns `404 NOT_FOUND`. The census is derived from the router (via `collectRoutes` in `api/src/platform/http/route-table.js:15`) so that a route added later either enters the census automatically or trips the "uncovered route" failure the census exists to catch. Staff subjects (`admin`, `agent`) are **not** restricted by ownership; the test pins both halves.

**Not in scope:** any web/android UI, the customer portal, reply/messages routes (owned by `CONVERSATION-*`; if the route does not exist yet, the census gains it when it arrives — that is the point), roles other than customer and staff.

## Product rules (from story)

- **SC-1** — one organisation, one queue: **staff are not restricted by ownership**. An `admin` or `agent` subject acts on any ticket.
- **SC-2** — every rule is enforced in the API; **no client enforces anything**. The guard lives in the service, not in a route middleware and not in the web app.
- **404, not 403** — a refusal that distinguishes "not yours" from "not there" tells a stranger that somebody else's ticket exists. Same status (`404`), same code (`'NOT_FOUND'`), same body as the existing "row not found" refusals at `tickets.service.js:212` and `:247`.
- **Customer subjects may not exist yet.** Whether a customer can hold a token today depends on `IDENTITY-*` and on `I-1` (`customers.user_id` nullable until first sign-in). Build the guard against a subject whose `role === 'customer'` regardless — a guard that waits for its first caller arrives after the hole.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Add the ownership guard inside the transaction that already reads the ticket

**File:** `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js`

In `assign(actor, { id, assigneeId, revision })` at line 194, immediately **after** the `if (!before) throw new HttpError(404, 'NOT_FOUND');` at line 212 (i.e. once `before` is known to exist), add:

```js
// Customers act on their own tickets only. A refusal that distinguished
// "not yours" from "not there" would tell a stranger somebody else's
// ticket exists (SC-2). Same status, same code, same body as line 212.
if (actor.role === 'customer' && before.customer_id !== actor.customerId) {
  throw new HttpError(404, 'NOT_FOUND');
}
```

Do the **same** in `changeStatus(actor, { id, status, revision, note })` at line 239, immediately after the `if (!before) throw new HttpError(404, 'NOT_FOUND');` at line 247.

Notes for the executor:
- Read what field the subject exposes for the customer link (grep `identity.subject-resolver.js`, `identity.service.js`, `identity.repository.js` for the resolved subject shape — the field may be `customerId`, `customer_id`, `subjectId`, or nested; use whatever the resolver actually attaches, **do not invent one**). If the resolver does not yet expose the customer link, add it there in the same commit and cite the resolver line in the PR description.
- The row field on `before` is `customer_id` (see `api/src/platform/db/migrations/0001__customers.sql` and the tickets table in `0002__tickets.sql`). Confirm by grepping `customer_id` in `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.repository.js` before writing.
- **Do not** wrap this in a helper that lives in the route file. **Do not** add route-level middleware. Four copies of one rule in four routes is what the census below exists to catch.
- **Do not** add a separate SELECT for the check — reuse `before`, which is already loaded inside the transaction.

### 2 — Extend the guard when `read` / `history` / other `/tickets/:id/*` service methods land

**Rule to state in the plan for future contributors** (add as a comment above the `assign` guard, one line):

> A new service method that takes `actor` and an `id` under `/tickets/:id` runs the same three-line ownership check inside its transaction, immediately after the row-not-found refusal. The census in `ticket-ownership.guarantee.test.js` fails until it does.

### 3 — Add the route-enumeration census test

**Create file:** `api/src/features/tickets/ticket-ownership.guarantee.test.js`

Model the file on `api/src/features/audit/audit.guarantee.test.js`:

```js
// A customer may act only on their own ticket. This file is the enforcement
// test for SC-2 on that rule: every route the ticket router serves under
// /tickets/:id is exercised here as a non-owner customer subject, and each
// one must refuse with 404 NOT_FOUND — indistinguishable from the row not
// existing, so the refusal does not confirm somebody else's ticket exists.
//
// The set of routes checked is DERIVED FROM THE ROUTER, not listed here.
// A route added later either enters the census automatically (because the
// enumeration test walks the router) or trips the "uncovered route" failure
// this census exists to catch.

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import express from 'express';
import { collectRoutes } from '../../platform/http/route-table.js';
import { ticketsRouter } from './tickets.routes.js';
// ...harness imports mirroring assign.test.js / status.test.js

const READ_ONLY_METHODS = new Set(['HEAD', 'OPTIONS']);

// Every route under /tickets/:id that this file drives as a non-owner
// customer. Compared against the router below — listing a route here
// without driving it satisfies the census with a claim rather than a test,
// which is the failure the census exists to prevent (see the audit
// guarantee's identical comment).
const EXERCISED = new Set([
  'PATCH /tickets/:id/assignee',
  'PATCH /tickets/:id/status',
  // GET /tickets/:id, PATCH /tickets/:id/messages, GET /tickets/:id/history
  // enter here the day the router serves them AND this file drives them.
]);
```

Then three tests:

1. **`every route under /tickets/:id the router serves is exercised by this file`** — mount `ticketsRouter({ db, now })` on an `express()` app, call `collectRoutes(app, '')`, filter to entries whose path matches `/tickets/:id` (i.e. starts with `/tickets/:id` and is not exactly `/tickets`), drop `READ_ONLY_METHODS`, then:
   - `uncovered = served − EXERCISED` — fail with `` `ownership guard not exercised for: ${uncovered.join(', ')}` `` (mirror the audit test's message at line 87).
   - `stale = EXERCISED − served` — fail with `` `exercised route no longer served: ${stale.join(', ')}` `` (mirror line 90).

   > **`GET /tickets/:id` note.** The census filters `HEAD`/`OPTIONS` only, **not** `GET` — the intake says "when they read it, then it is refused" and the ownership rule applies to reads as well. The moment a read route lands, this test forces it into `EXERCISED` and into the driven cases below.

2. **`each route under /tickets/:id refuses a non-owner customer with 404 NOT_FOUND`** — for each entry in `EXERCISED`, drive it with a request whose subject is a customer who does **not** own the target ticket. Assert `res.status === 404` and `res.body.code === 'NOT_FOUND'`. Assert the response body **equals** the body returned when the ticket id does not exist at all (mint a fresh uuid, call the same route, deep-equal the two responses). This is the "does not confirm somebody else's ticket exists" half of the first criterion.

3. **`each route under /tickets/:id accepts a staff subject on any ticket (SC-1)`** — for each entry in `EXERCISED`, drive it with an `admin` and an `agent` subject against a ticket they do not own; assert the response is not `404 NOT_FOUND`. (The specific success/failure varies per route — an `assign` may still 400 on a bad `assigneeId` — but it must not be the ownership refusal.) This pins the "staff are not restricted" half so a future guard change that widens the block cannot pass silently.

Add the comment that made the audit census work (paraphrased from `audit.guarantee.test.js:113–122`): naming a route in `EXERCISED` without actually driving it satisfies the census with a claim; the driving tests are what turn the claim into a test.

### 4 — No new route added by this story

State plainly in the PR body: this story adds **no** route. `GET /tickets/:id` and reply/history routes are out of scope (owned by other stories). The census is designed to fail loudly the day one of them lands without an ownership guard, which is the whole point.

### 5 — Frontend / Android

**No frontend changes required.** SC-2 forbids any client enforcement; this story only tightens the API. The web queue in `web/src/pages/tickets/TicketQueuePage.tsx` already receives `404` from the API on missing tickets and needs no code change.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Customer subject cannot yet be minted in production.** If `IDENTITY-*` does not yet issue a token whose resolved subject has `role === 'customer'`, the guard is dead code at runtime but the census still fires against a **test-only** subject (see task 3). Do not skip the test on that ground: the rule is "no client enforces anything", and a guard that waits for its first caller is a guard that arrives after the hole. Enforced in `api/src/features/tickets/tickets.service.js` at the new checks after lines 212 and 247.
- **Customer subject with `customerId === null`** (a signed-in user not yet linked to a customer row — see `I-1`). The guard treats `null !== before.customer_id` as "not yours" and returns `404 NOT_FOUND`. Add a driven case for this in the census test.
- **Staff subject (`admin` or `agent`) on any ticket.** Guard is skipped; behaviour matches the queue this sprint's predecessor shipped. Pinned by task 3 test 3.
- **Unknown role** (any role that is neither `customer` nor `admin` / `agent`). The guard's condition `actor.role === 'customer'` intentionally lets unknown roles through unblocked because the token issuer (`identity`) is authoritative for which roles exist; a role that leaks past the resolver is an identity bug, not a ticket bug. Note this explicitly in the guard comment so a future reviewer does not "helpfully" invert it.
- **Route added later under `/tickets/:id`** without an ownership check. Census test 1 fails with "ownership guard not exercised for: <route>", forcing either an `EXERCISED` entry (and its driven cases in tests 2 and 3) or an explicit waiver (deliberately not offered in this file — the intake wants no waivers).
- **Route removed later.** Stale check in test 1 fails with "exercised route no longer served", forcing the `EXERCISED` set to shrink.
- **`GET /tickets` (queue list) response leaking foreign tickets to a customer.** Out of scope for this story per the intake (the queue is `SC-1` staff-first). Document as follow-up in the PR body; do **not** silently patch `list` here.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] A customer subject reading, mutating, or otherwise acting on a ticket that is not theirs receives `404 NOT_FOUND` with a body byte-identical to the body returned for a ticket id that does not exist.
- [ ] Every route the ticket router serves under `/tickets/:id` (currently `PATCH /tickets/:id/assignee` and `PATCH /tickets/:id/status`) is exercised as a non-owner customer in `ticket-ownership.guarantee.test.js` and refuses `404 NOT_FOUND`.
- [ ] The census test derives the set of routes from `collectRoutes(app, '')` (per `api/src/platform/http/route-table.js:15`) and fails loudly when a route is added, removed, or renamed without a matching guard.
- [ ] `admin` and `agent` subjects act on any ticket regardless of ownership; both roles are pinned by a driven test case (SC-1).
- [ ] The ownership check lives inside the transaction that already reads the row (in `tickets.service.js` after `before` is loaded), not in `tickets.routes.js` and not in shared middleware.
- [ ] No web, Android, or route-file changes are shipped for this story.
- [ ] `cd api && npm test` passes; `cd web && npm run build` still passes on the unchanged web tree.
- [ ] Nothing in the diff, commit messages, or file contents mentions AI assistance (`git diff | grep -iE 'copilot|chatgpt|claude|assistant|ai[- ]generated'` is empty).
